clue.text: Bad dress rehearsal? Then there's another thing — l-light's out!

definitions.text: Bad dress rehearsal? Then there's another thing — l-light's out!

parts.note: surface reading: a theatre company's final run-through has gone badly

parts.words: Then there's another thing — l-light's out!
parts.note: setter's reading: the stammered 'l-light' and lights going out point to the theatre saying that a bad rehearsal means a good opening, and to bedtime

explanation.surface: A nervous actor stammers after a shambolic dress rehearsal, consoling themselves before the lights go down.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre folk say a bad dress rehearsal means a good first performance; the answer is the reassuring phrase they use. 'Lights out' also hints at night-time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock theatrical reassurance that problems in rehearsal will vanish once the real performance starts.

clue.text: … for the boys I yell with horribly

definitions.note: elliptical: completes 'Two, two, the lily-white boys' from the counting song

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched and messed about, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, though it also reads as a joining word

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a group of boys in a terrible way.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue 1 Across's 'Green Grow the Rushes, O', an English folk counting song: 'Two, two, the lily-white boys'. 'with' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the counting song the second verse names the lily-white boys, so the adjective is what goes 'for the boys'.

clue.text: … for more than this 5 in retreat from below

definitions.note: elliptical: the song's verse is 'Three, three, the rivals', the plural being more than this singular

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means reading upwards, back to front
the number sits in, inside, the word for a retreat

explanation.surface: A cryptic continuation of the counting song, with something retreating upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a reference to 5 Down, but here it is just the Roman numeral. The counting song's third verse is 'Three, three, the rivals'.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor for the same prize; the song uses the plural, so one of them is less than the full verse.

clue.text: … for their makers: leave a lot of enchantments

definitions.note: elliptical: the song's verse is 'Four for the gospel makers'

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so one letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A cryptic continuation of the counting song, about leaving behind most of some magic.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls in the charms word is the part not taken. The counting song's fourth verse is 'Four for the gospel makers', the four evangelists.
explanation.definitionFit: The four evangelists Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote the books of Christian scripture, so these are what they made.

clue.text: Die, sadly, during excursion — a current affair

indicators.note: something happening during an outing sits inside it
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the word before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dies on an outing, reported like a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current affair' sounds like news, but here it is literal: an affair involving a current of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide rip is a stretch of turbulent water where opposing currents meet, literally a matter of currents.

clue.text: Large number or small number, nothing to a celebrity

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, as in a literary lion; 'to' places it next

explanation.surface: A comparison of big and small numbers, nothing next to a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is ten to the thirtieth power in modern usage, an enormous figure.

clue.text: William of Orange?

parts.note: surface reading: the Dutch prince who became King William III of England
setter's reading: the first name of the Tory leader of 1999, whose surname is also the Dutch city where the House of Orange holds court

explanation.walkthrough: In 1999 William Hague led Britain's Conservative Party; the Dutch royal house of Orange governs from the city with the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of politician William Hague matches the Dutch seat of government associated with the Orange dynasty.

clue.text: Exclamation applied to scenes worth broadcasting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dated British cry of astonishment

definitions.note: cryptic: what you do to birds in fields where seed is broadcast
definitions.meaning: second meaning: broadcasting is sowing seed by scattering it, and birds raiding such fields get pelted

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in astonishment at something sensational enough for the evening news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' looks like television; it is the farmer's scattering of seed, which birds come to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated British cry of astonishment and also, literally, pelting birds that eat scattered seed.

clue.text: Standing at the door after 2, 3 and 4, they are shown off

parts.note: in the counting song the verse after two, three and four is 'Five for the symbols at your door'

explanation.surface: People stand in a doorway after a sequence of numbers, being displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Grow the Rushes, O' is an English folk counting song; clues 2, 3 and 4 Down quote its verses, and the fifth is 'Five for the symbols at your door'.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions bought to display wealth or rank are flaunted to impress others, which is their whole purpose.

clue.text: Prepared to drive without trousers, for all the world to see

definitions.text: for all the world to see

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the golf word wraps round the clothing

parts.note: in golf you tee up the ball before driving

explanation.surface: A golfer lines up a drive with no trousers on, in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shown on television is broadcast so that a mass audience everywhere can watch it.

clue.text: See 1
Recently elevated to indoor post

parts.note: EL is the American short name for an elevated railway

explanation.surface: Someone recently promoted to a job inside the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job; it is a wooden upright.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the upright pillar at the foot or turn of a staircase that supports the handrail inside a house.

clue.text: Provide me with 50-tonner for the making of joined-up characters

definitions.note: loose: the answer is the act that makes people into joined-up characters

indicators.note: the given letters are raw material from which something new is made

explanation.surface: A request for a heavy lorry to help with joined-up handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined-up characters' looks like cursive script; read as people who have joined up, it means signing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing on as a member or recruit makes you someone who has joined up, so this is the process of joining.

clue.text: Religious revellers — this includes one American

indicators.note: one word includes, holds within it, the next

explanation.surface: A group of worshipping partygoers that includes one person from America.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a thiasus was a band of worshippers, typically celebrating Dionysus with revelry.

clue.text: Some fish forks partly caught in a shoe by the 3s' companion

definitions.note: a play described by its author

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, its tail cut away

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short

indicators.note: the cricket letter sits in, inside, the footwear

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Fish, cutlery and a shoe tumble together, like a strange still life.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 Down is RIVAL, so the 3s are The Rivals, Sheridan's play; his other famous comedy is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote both comedies, so this play is a companion piece to The Rivals by the same playwright.

clue.text: Drink embracing a couple returning from fertility god

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole is read right to left
the drink word wraps its arms round the couple

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink while hugging two people who are coming back from a pagan deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapus was the Greek god of fertility, gardens and livestock, famous for his oversized phallus.

clue.text: Let Dad run round with spirit

indicators.note: the running word goes round, encircling the first word

explanation.surface: A father is allowed to jog around carrying a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like alcohol; it is the Holy Spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian theology the Paraclete, meaning advocate or comforter, is a title of the Holy Spirit.

clue.text: First lady's got meat in place of plums

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Eve swaps fruit for meat, a twist on the Eden story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' looks like 'instead of'; the definition is just 'place of plums'. Evesham is an English market town whose vale is famous for plum orchards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Evesham in Worcestershire is England's best-known plum-growing district, so the town is a home of the fruit.

clue.text: Despicable commercials for audience of 14

definitions.note: elliptical: members of a band of religious revellers, 14 Across

indicators.note: put before an audience, so heard rather than read

parts.note: mean is despicable, ads are commercials

explanation.surface: Nasty adverts are being shown to a viewership.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were frenzied female followers of Dionysus, the women who made up his band of worshippers.

clue.text: Co-operation to show New York's grey

indicators.note: the letters are put on show in a new display, rearranged

parts.note: NY is New York, plus the S

explanation.surface: A claim that teamwork reveals the dull colour of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means combined action by parts working together to produce more than they would achieve separately.

clue.text: See 15
Fabulous bird on the hill: time for Tommy, perhaps

parts.note: the giant bird of Arabian legend
kop is a South African word for hill; 'on' puts the bird first

explanation.surface: A mythical bird perches on a hillside: time for a British soldier, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' looks like a British soldier; it is The Who's 1969 album telling a story in songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who's Tommy is the most famous example of a story told entirely through rock music, so it is one instance.

clue.text: Pastry? Tell it to go away!

indicators.note: to tell is to say out loud, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: what you say to make an animal go away

explanation.surface: A cake has annoyed someone, who wants it gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The French light pastry used for eclairs and profiteroles is pronounced exactly like the scaring-away word.

clue.text: Bill's in employment with sheep

indicators.note: the bill sits in, inside, the employment word

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is working with sheep, like a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account. Jacob is also the Bible shepherd who tended Laban's flocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacob is a piebald, often four-horned British breed of sheep, named after the patriarch.

clue.text: Article grasped by black girl

indicators.note: something grasped is held inside another's grip

explanation.surface: A dark-haired girl clutches an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a common female first name, so it serves as one example of a girl.

clue.text: Lanolin at a loss in Virginia

indicators.note: read as 'at' being lost, those two letters go

parts.note: wool fat is another name for lanolin

explanation.surface: Someone in the state of Virginia is baffled by lanolin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a loss' looks like 'baffled'; split it as 'at' plus loss. 'Virginia' looks like the US state but is the writer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf was the English modernist novelist, so her first name points to her surname.

clue.text: Composer to put on inches and a greater measure

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches, much greater than an inch

explanation.surface: A composer is told to gain weight around the waist, and more.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Addinsell was the British composer of the Warsaw Concerto.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Addinsell wrote film music including the Warsaw Concerto for Dangerous Moonlight in 1941.

clue.text: Say part of the word for special delivery

parts.note: a word is made of letters

explanation.surface: Utter a fragment of a word to mean a premium postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal item sent by a faster, premium service is delivered separately and urgently, which is what special delivery offers.
